1 SECTION 1. MAVIC4PRO 100×100 — STATIC SCAN Mavic4Pro 100 m altitude × 100 m distance realtime_yolo11_sdr.py 0 0 0 The fixed scan proves that Mavic4Pro is detectable when the SDR is tuned to the correct frequency.
2 SECTION 2. MAVIC4PRO 100×100 — ORIGINAL MULTIBAND Mavic4Pro 100 m altitude × 100 m distance realtime_ia_multiband.py 0 0 4 The original multiband scan shows clues, but does not sustain enough evidence to confirm the drone.
3 SECTION 3. MAVIC4PRO 50×50 — STATIC SCAN Mavic4Pro 50 m altitude × 50 m distance realtime_yolo11_sdr.py 0 0 0 At short range, the fixed scan repeatedly detects Mavic4Pro, confirming that the RF signature is present.
4 SECTION 4. MAVIC4PRO 50×50 — ORIGINAL MULTIBAND Mavic4Pro 50 m altitude × 50 m distance realtime_ia_multiband.py 0 0 3 The original multiband scan can detect some evidence, but it is less reliable than fixed-frequency scanning.
5 SECTION 5. AUTEL — RANGE TESTS Autel: 50×50 up to 500×1000 realtime_yolo11_sdr.py / realtime_ia_multiband.py 28 0 71 This block shows gradual degradation with range and helps compare fixed-frequency vs. multiband behavior.
6 SECTION 6. MAVIC4PRO — UPDATED ORIGINAL MULTIBAND RANGE TESTS Mavic4Pro: 50×50 up to 200×400 realtime_ia_multiband.py 108 0 150 This block documents how the original multiband logic behaves across increasing Mavic4Pro range scenarios.
7 SECTION 7. MAVIC4PRO 200×400 — V2 MULTIBAND GAIN COMPARISON Mavic4Pro 200 m altitude × 400 m distance realtime_ia_v2_multiband.py 86 108 118 The key result is that 30 dB already confirms the drone, showing that the v2 decision logic matters more than only increasing gain.
8 SECTION 8. MAVIC4PRO 200×500 — ORIGINAL MULTIBAND BASELINE Mavic4Pro 200 m altitude × 500 m distance realtime_ia_multiband.py 1 0 6 This block works as a comparison point before switching again to the improved v2 scanner.
9 SECTION 9. MAVIC4PRO 200×500 — V2 EXTENDED STRESS TEST Mavic4Pro 200 m altitude × 500 m distance realtime_ia_v2_multiband.py 48 81 62 This is an upper-range stress test to evaluate the practical limit of the improved detector.
